summary: 76-year-old man with recurrent sigmoid volvulus, now peritonism, T 38.6 °C, HR 124, BP 88/54, drowsy, lactate 5.2; CT: non-enhancing sigmoid wall, pneumatosis, free gas.

inputs.hpi: 3 days of distension and no flatus; since last night constant severe lower abdominal pain, fever and rigors, now drowsy. Previous sigmoid volvulus decompressed endoscopically 8 months ago; declined elective surgery.

exam.general: Drowsy, peripherally cool. Temperature 38.6°C, pulse 124/min, BP 88/54, RR 26.
exam.abdomen: Tense distension with peritonism, guarding and rebound in the left iliac fossa and lower abdomen. Bowel sounds absent.

imaging.name: CT abdomen/pelvis with IV contrast
imaging.result: Sigmoid volvulus with absent enhancement of the sigmoid wall, pneumatosis and free fluid — gangrene. Small volume free gas.

surgicalHistory: Endoscopic decompression of sigmoid volvulus (8 months ago)

confirmedDiagnosis.name: Gangrenous sigmoid volvulus with peritonitis
confirmedDiagnosis.assessmentText: Sigmoid volvulus with gangrene, perforation and peritonitis, septic shock. Emergency laparotomy — Hartmann's procedure. No endoscopic detorsion.

mustExclude.note: Endoscopic detorsion is contraindicated with peritonitis, gangrene or perforation.

guideline.name: ASCRS clinical practice guidelines — colonic volvulus and acute colonic pseudo-obstruction
guideline.section: Sigmoid volvulus: endoscopic detorsion without peritonitis/ischaemia, then sigmoid colectomy during the same admission; emergency resection for gangrene/perforation; caecal volvulus: operative management, endoscopic reduction not recommended
guideline.citation: Alavi K, Poylin V, Davids JS, et al. The American Society of Colon and Rectal Surgeons clinical practice guidelines for the management of colonic volvulus and acute colonic pseudo-obstruction. Dis Colon Rectum. 2021;64:1046–57.

guideline.name: WSES consensus guidelines — sigmoid volvulus management
guideline.section: Endoscopic decompression when no peritonitis/ischaemia; emergency surgery (Hartmann's) for gangrene, perforation or failed decompression; elective sigmoidectomy after decompression
guideline.citation: Tian BWCA, Vigutto G, Tan E, et al. WSES consensus guidelines on sigmoid volvulus management. World J Emerg Surg. 2023;18:34.

guideline.name: Surviving Sepsis Campaign — international guidelines for sepsis and septic shock 2021
guideline.section: Screening (do not use qSOFA alone), antibiotics within 1 h of shock, blood cultures, lactate, 30 mL/kg crystalloid for hypoperfusion, vasopressors, source control
guideline.citation: Evans L, Rhodes A, Alhazzani W, et al. Surviving Sepsis Campaign: international guidelines for management of sepsis and septic shock 2021. Crit Care Med. 2021;49:e1063–e1143.

rationale: Permutation: severity. Gangrenous volvulus with septic shock needs resuscitation and emergency Hartmann's; endoscopic detorsion is contraindicated.
